extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; scholars and practitioners interested in sovereignty, civil obligation, and the limits of government
extracted.subtask_description: Normative rules and distinctions governing liberty, obligation, and the powers of sovereigns and subordinate bodies — i.e., when subjects may act freely, when covenants bind them, and what counts as the acts or liabilities of representatives or assemblies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of liberty (liberty of the man vs. of faculties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty signifies the absence of external impediment to a man's actions; when we say someone 'speaks freely' or a 'gift is free' it refers to the liberty of the person (the giver/speaker) rather than liberty of the object or faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The way is free' means those who walk in it are not stopped; 'Freewill' implies liberty of the man (finding no stop in doing what he wills), not a metaphysical freedom of the will detached from causes. Use 'liberty' to mean absence of external impediment, not an ontological freedom of faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear and liberty are consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions done out of fear (e.g., throwing goods into the sea to save a ship) can still be actions of a man at liberty because no one hinders him from refusing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish voluntary actions motivated by fear from actions compelled by physical restraint; being motivated by fear does not negate that the agent acted voluntarily and with liberty, though the action may be dishonourable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty and necessity are consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary actions proceed from the will (liberty) yet also proceed from causes in a continual chain (necessity); to an observer seeing the chain of causes, voluntary acts appear necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reconciles human liberty with causal determinism: the will's liberty (acting according to desire) coexists with the necessity that desires have causes. Use this to deny that liberty implies indeterminism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil laws are artificial bonds created by covenant
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil laws are 'Artificiall Chains' fastened by mutual covenants to the lips of the sovereign and to the ears of subjects; they are weak in nature but made to hold by the danger of breaking them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat laws as humanly instituted obligations whose binding force depends on enforcement and the risk of punishment rather than metaphysical necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty of subjects consists in what the sovereign praetermits
rubrics_metrics.description: The liberty of a subject is limited to those things the sovereign has not regulated; subjects retain freedom to do what the laws omit, e.g., buy and sell, choose abode, diet, trade, and educate their children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate natural corporeal liberty or exemption from all laws with the liberty of subjects under commonwealth; measure subjects' liberty by the scope of actions left unregulated by sovereign law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty of subjects compatible with unlimited sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign may have power of life and death over subjects; such acts are not 'injury' to subjects in the juridical sense because subjects authorized the sovereign by covenant — the moral guilt may lie before God but not as an injustice from sovereign to subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the legal/constitutional distinction: sovereign actions, even if contrary to natural equity, are not injuries to subjects insofar as subjects authorized sovereign power; examples include biblical and historical cases (Jeptha, David).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public or republican 'liberty' praised by ancients is liberty of commonwealths, not private men
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who praise 'liberty' (Greeks and Romans) mean the liberty of the commonwealth (the state) to act independently, not the private liberty of individuals within it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware the misleading application of classical 'liberty' to private individuals; civic liberty historically often refers to the independence or freedoms of states, which can coexist with severe constraints on individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure subjects' obligation and liberty by words of submission or the institution's end
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation and liberty of a subject must be inferred either from express words of consent ('I Authorise all his Actions') or from the intention/end for which sovereignty was instituted (peace and defence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether a subject remains free to omit an act, check explicit contractual language or whether obedience is necessary to achieve the institution's end; ambiguous grants are interpreted by purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects are not bound to hurt themselves or surrender life-saving means when commanded
rubrics_metrics.description: Covenants not to defend one's own body are void; if sovereign commands a subject to kill or wound themselves or to abstain from food/medicine without which they cannot live, they have liberty to disobey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-preservation cannot be surrendered by covenant; apply this to refuse sovereign commands that require self-harm. Also: a subject is not obliged to confess a crime without assurance of pardon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects not obliged to engage in warfare unless they voluntarily undertook it
rubrics_metrics.description: One commanded as a soldier may in many cases refuse unless he voluntarily enlisted or took impress money; substitution by providing a sufficient soldier preserves non-desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for voluntary enlistment and contracts: those who undertake military service are bound to fight and not flee without leave; natural cowardice excuses some conduct unless contractually removed by enlistment or impressed pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: No liberty to resist sovereign in defence of another (except in special circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resistance to the commonwealth's sword to defend another (guilty or innocent) is not permitted as it undermines the sovereign's means of protection; however if many have already unjustly resisted, subsequent joint defence of their persons can be self-preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish initial unlawful breach (which is unjust) from later acts of self-defence by those already condemned; note that offer of pardon removes the plea of self-defence for continuing resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects' greatest liberty depends on the silence of the law
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the sovereign prescribes no rule, the subject has liberty to act or forbear; therefore liberties vary by place and time according to what the sovereign thinks convenient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the silence or expressness of legal rules to locate freedoms (e.g., earlier English liberty of forcible entry later removed by statute). Where law is silent, subjects may act per their discretion until sovereign decides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects may sue sovereign on grounds of statutory/precedent law
rubrics_metrics.description: If the sovereign demands by force of a former law (not by use of sovereign power), the subject has liberty to sue for right before judges appointed by the sovereign according to that law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate claims against sovereign as administrator of law (actionable under the law being enforced) from claims against sovereign's exercise of sovereign power (which are not actionable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants inconsistent with sovereign's ability to provide safety are void
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sovereign grants liberties that disable him from providing for subjects' safety (e.g., powers necessary to exercise sovereignty), such grants are void unless he explicitly renounces or transfers sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret grants against the preservation of sovereign power as errors of ignorance and void; sovereign retains necessary powers like war, judicature, appointing officers, levying money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects' obligation lasts only as long as sovereign's power to protect them
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation of subjects to the sovereign endures no longer than the sovereign's ability to protect them; if the sovereign loses the power of protection, subjects return to natural liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat protection as the end of obedience: where protection ceases (violent overthrow, incapacity, or loss of sovereign), obligation dissolves and natural right of self-preservation reasserts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Captivity and voluntary acceptance of victor's terms transfers subjection
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject taken prisoner who accepts conditions to preserve life becomes subject to the victor; but a person detained without consent is not bound by covenant and may escape by any means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent in extremis (accepting terms to save life) effects lawful transfer of allegiance; lack of consent to detention leaves liberty to escape.

rubrics_metrics.name: If sovereign relinquishes sovereignty, subjects revert to natural liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: If a monarch relinquishes sovereignty for himself and his heirs (or dies without heir), subjects return to the absolute liberty of the state of nature because no sovereign remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sovereign abdication or death without heir dissolves subjection; absence of declared heir means no lawful subjection continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banishment suspends subjection during exile
rubrics_metrics.description: A subject banished is not a subject during the banishment; but a person sent on a message or travelling with leave remains a subject (their exception is by contract between sovereigns, not by release from domestic covenant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish punitive exile (suspends subjection) from licensed travel (remains subject). Privileges abroad depend on inter-sovereign agreements or special license.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a sovereign becomes subject to another by conquest, subjects' obligations transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: If a monarch subdued by war renders himself subject to the victor, his subjects are delivered from former obligation and become obliged to the victor; but if the monarch is merely held prisoner without consent, original right remains and the former magistrates continue to govern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate voluntary submission by sovereign from captivity without consent; only the former transfers lawful sovereignty and hence subjects' obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and classification of 'Systemes' (regular/irregular, politicall/private, lawful/unlawful)
rubrics_metrics.description: SYSTEMES are numbers of men joined in one interest or business; Regular systemes have a representative (some absolute and independent, some dependent), irregular consist only in concourse. Private systemes may be lawfull or unlawfull depending on commonwealth allowance and intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to judge the legality and nature of associations: determine whether a body has legitimate representation, derived authority, and whether its purpose or number renders it unlawful (e.g., threatening, secret, or malintent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative power of bodies politique limited by sovereign
rubrics_metrics.description: In all bodies politique the power of the representative is always limited by the sovereign; what prescribes those limits is either the letters (writ) or the laws of the commonwealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the scope of a representative's authority by consulting its commission (letters patents) and the ordinary laws; any power beyond those bounds is not the act of the body as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of letters patents to define limitations of subordinate bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Subordinate bodies need written letters (patents, sealed) to record and make permanent the limitations necessary for their business, times, and places; unwritten limitations may be indeterminate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require formal written commissions for subordinate corporations so members and outsiders can read and know their authority; where writings are silent, ordinary laws must supply rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwarranted acts by a single representative are his own, not the body's
rubrics_metrics.description: If the representative is one man, whatsoever he does beyond his letters or the laws is his own act and not that of the body or other members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold single representatives personally liable for acts beyond their commission; validate acts only within the scope of letters and law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unwarranted acts by an assembly are acts only of those who assented
rubrics_metrics.description: When the representative is an assembly, acts not warranted by letters or laws are the acts of the assembly and of every member who voted for the decree, but not of those who voted contrary or were absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine corporate liability by who voted for a measure; innocent dissenters are not authors of unauthorized acts and are not culpable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for debts when representative is one man
rubrics_metrics.description: If the person of the body politique is in one man who borrows money of a stranger, the debt is the representative's alone; members are not obliged unless the letters entitle that representative to bind them (which would amount to sovereignty).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creditors must look to the person who contracted; do not assume communal liability absent explicit authority in the commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability for debts when representative is an assembly
rubrics_metrics.description: When the representative is an assembly and a debt to a stranger is contracted, only those who gave their votes to the borrowing or to the contract are responsible for the debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish who voted for the borrowing to determine who is obligated; an author of the borrowing may be obliged for the whole debt though one pay it and be discharged.

rubrics_metrics.name: If debt is to a member of the assembly, the body only is obliged
rubrics_metrics.description: If the debt is to one of the assembly, the assembly alone is obliged to pay from common stock; a member who voted to lend cannot demand payment from particular members but only from the common treasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members who vote to lend become effectively both borrower and lender and cannot seek recourse against individual members beyond the corporation's resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protestation lawful against subordinate bodies but never against sovereign power
rubrics_metrics.description: It is sometimes lawful and expedient for a person to make protestation and record dissent against decrees of subordinate representative assemblies, but protesting a sovereign assembly denies their sovereignty and is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage protestation and recorded dissent within subordinate bodies to preserve personal liberty from mistaken collective acts; forbid such protestation where it would amount to denying sovereign authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of provincial/colonial/town bodies politique
rubrics_metrics.description: Assemblies governing provinces, colonies, towns, universities, colleges, or churches have power limited by their commissions and cannot execute power beyond their territorial bounds; debts and unlawful acts are the acts of those who assented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not recognize acts or execution of jurisdiction by an assembly outside its territorial remit; remedies for injury by such bodies belong to the sovereign's courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative form for trade and the monopoly effect of incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: For ordering foreign traffic, the most commodious representative is an assembly of all adventurers; granting corporate monopoly to a company creates a 'double Monopoly' (sole buyers at home and sole sellers abroad) beneficial to merchants but disadvantageous to the people at home and foreigners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate incorporation and trade monopolies by their distributive effects: they can raise home prices and reduce competition, harming domestic consumers and foreign trade partners. Prefer assemblies inclusive of adventurers to better serve common interests.
